findings.rule: REQ-03-018 — "IF the day columns at their minimum width are wider than the space available, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL scroll the grid horizontally"; time-off/01 contracts §Screens — "the day columns divide what is left"
findings.claim: `min-width: max-content` is not the sum of the column floors: under it a day column takes the width of the widest content in ANY day column, so one whole-view holiday name in a header inflates all 30 columns of the Month window and makes the shipped Month/Week/2-weeks views scroll at a desktop viewport — a change to already-shipped geometry the spec did not ask for

witness.detail: Reproduce with the state TC-01-E2E-04 already builds (e2e/tests/time-off-calendar.spec.ts:396-414): an org holiday on 2026-09-21 named 'Company Day' with countryCode null, so `appliesToAllInView` is true, the Month window on September 2026, default 1280px viewport. CalendarScreen.tsx:530-536 then renders `Company Day` inside `calendar-day-header-2026-09-21`, and every row's template is `var(--name-col) repeat(30, minmax(var(--day-col-min), 1fr))` (CalendarScreen.tsx:290-291). Before this diff `.time-off-calendar-grid` had NO min-width at >=1200px, so the available space was definite and the fr tracks divided it: each day column ~29px and the holiday name wrapped inside it. This diff moves `min-width: max-content` out of `@media (max-width: 1199px)` and applies it at every width (globals.css:990-995), which makes the available space INDEFINITE for the row's track sizing. CSS Grid 12.7.1 (find the size of an fr, indefinite free space) takes the maximum over, among others, 'for each grid item that crosses a flexible track, the result of finding the size of an fr using ... a space to fill of the item's max-content contribution'. The holiday header is a single-track item with flex factor 1, and max-content ignores soft-wrap opportunities, so its contribution is the one-line width of 'Company Day' — about 60px at --font-size-xs. The used flex fraction becomes ~60, and because every day track is the same `minmax(--day-col-min, 1fr)`, ALL 30 columns become ~60px: 264 + 30*60 = ~2064px inside a ~1150px content area. The reader of a month with one holiday now sees about 14 of its 30 days and must scroll for the rest. The same happens for every window and every whole-view holiday; 'Independence Day' (spec 01/02's own example, and the sample body in contracts §Routes) is ~95px per column, ~3100px for a month. This is not what the rule under it says it does — globals.css:991-994 states 'the day columns take their own minimum (--day-col-min) and the container above scrolls once the sum of them is wider than the page' — nor what REQ-03-018 conditions the scroll on, nor Edge case 13 ('Every day column is at its minimum width and the grid scrolls'). No case catches it: TC-03-E2E-13 measures the floor and the scroll on a 92-day range with no holiday in it (both hold there, because with no item over 32px the fr fraction is the base size), and TC-01-E2E-04 asserts only colours and text presence, which survive any width. The 92-day range this spec exists for is unaffected and correct; what regressed is the three windows that already shipped.

findings.suggestedFix: Make the minimum the sum of the floors instead of the content: drop `min-width: max-content` and give the grid a computed floor from the day count the screen already knows — e.g. `style={{ minWidth: `calc(var(--name-col) + ${Math.max(days.length, 1)} * var(--day-col-min))` }}` on `.time-off-calendar-grid` (and the same on the skeleton's 14). The width is then definite at every viewport, columns divide the page when it is wide enough and sit exactly on `--day-col-min` when it is not, and TC-03-E2E-13's floor and scroll assertions hold unchanged. Extend TC-03-E2E-13 (or TC-01-E2E-04) with a day-header width read in a month that carries a whole-view holiday, so the state has a case.

dismissed: Review 1's L1 — CLOSED, checked against its own witness. `overflow: hidden` is gone from `.time-off-calendar-grid`; the border, radius and background moved onto `.time-off-calendar-scroll` (globals.css:983-988), which carries `overflow-x: auto` and is therefore the nearest scrollport ancestor of `.time-off-calendar-who` (globals.css:1019-1029, still `position: sticky; left: 0`). Nothing between the two establishes a scrollport: `.time-off-calendar-row` is `display: grid; position: relative` with no overflow, and `.time-off-calendar-grid` now carries `min-width` alone. A scroll container clips to its own rounded corners, so nothing replaces the removed `overflow: hidden`, and the frame now stays around the visible area instead of sliding off with a 3208px grid. TC-03-E2E-13 gained the assertion the finding said was missing (e2e/tests/time-off-calendar.spec.ts:821-848): it sets `container.scrollLeft = 400`, asserts the container really moved, and asserts the name cell is still within a pixel of the container's left edge — which is a case that fails on the old CSS and passes on the new.

The moved `background: var(--surface-page)` — a scroll container's background covers its padding box, which is the visible area, and the sticky name cell carries its own background at `z-index: 3` above the bands' `z-index: 2`, so the names still occlude the days scrolling under them. Nothing in the grid overflows vertically (bands are `height: var(--space-10)` inside `var(--space-12)` rows), so the `overflow-y: auto` that `overflow-x: auto` implies adds no scrollbar.

The new E2E assertions are not tautologies. `nameLeftAfter >= containerLeft - 1` fails by ~400px when the sticky cell is pinned to the wrong scrollport (the implement report records -83 against 316 on the previous commit), and `scrolled > 0` guards the case where the container did not scroll at all. `nameLeftBefore + 1` is the loose half of the pair and is carried for direction, not for detection.
`page.getByTestId('calendar-grid')` in TC-03-E2E-13 is not ambiguous where it is used — the range panel has closed by then (see L9 for the latent version of this).

`type Locator` is re-exported by e2e/tests/fixtures.ts:82, and `TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES` still has a consumer at time-off-calendar.spec.ts:648 after the two refusal assertions were deleted, so neither import is stale.

The rewritten TC-01-E2E-02 and TC-01-E2E-11 are not weakened cases (CR-24/CR-25): each replaces a refusal assertion the spec withdrew (REQ-03-003) with the positive assertion that replaces it — every member row visible, the banner absent, and in E2E-11 a third window's day headers disjoint from the second's, which is a stronger read of the stale-grid rule than the deleted one.

The `pageToDay` helper's six-click ceiling and the `Escape` re-arm in TC-03-E2E-12 are sound: DateRangePicker resets `pending` on close (DateRangePicker.tsx:120-123) and re-opens on `monthOf(start)` (:114-117), so the second pass finds the armed day rendered.

CR-01/CR-02/CR-03/CR-06 — the route's guards and scoping are untouched. resolveRows still filters on `caller.organizationId` (time-off-calendar.service.ts:310), which comes from the session, and the controller's guard pair is not in the diff. The widened default resolves to the same set the `all` scope already answered for the same roles.
CR-04 — no new authorization code; `seedMemberships` writes `role: 'user'` into a String column and its rows are listed, never used to authorize.
CR-21/CR-22 — no migration and no schema change.
CR-10 — no route handler and no server action; the one fetch keeps `credentials: 'same-origin'`.
CR-28 — no test in the diff pins a port or names devscribed_dev; TC-03-E2E-13 uses setViewportSize and the suite's own fixtures.

CR-31/CR-32 elsewhere — `maxSpanDays` is optional and the three shipped DateRangePicker consumers pass nothing; `TimeOffCalendarWindow` is unwidened and its two anchor functions are untouched; the deleted validation exports have no remaining consumer in apps, packages or e2e.
The `--day-col-min: 32px` literal is declared, not improvised: cases.md §DS gaps carries it as a named gap with the value's reason, which is the route CLAUDE.md prescribes.
The branch carries the spec's work and nothing else — `git diff --stat` over the base is exactly the nine files, and the two commits since review 1 touch only globals.css and the e2e case.
